column1: # Client manifest — the source of truth for which casinos this proxy serves.
# Applied to a VM with scripts/sync-clients-from-repo.sh, which regenerates
# /etc/proxies/clients/*.env and runs manage-clients.sh sync when something changed.
# Onboarding a brand is a one-line change and a pull request.
#   client       hostname label prefix = EGT casino identifier, lowercased,
#                underscore removed. Derive from the CASINOKEY, not the Casino
#                column: they differ where a brand was renamed.
#   casino_id    EGT casinokey. Reported as casinoId in the URL payload.
#   host_suffix  '-bgsp' or 'none'. Which naming form is advertised for this brand.
#                Both forms are always served; this only picks the advertised one.
#   enabled      yes / no. 'no' means do not create vhosts or a URL payload.
#   notes        free text, ignored by the sync script.
# Nothing here is secret: no credentials, no rotated domain. Those stay on the VM
# Verify a label before enabling it:
#   Any HTTP code = routes. 000 = does not route.
# Status below measured against p3 and p4. Re-measure before trusting it.
# Already migrated off the legacy suffix: dnpalacebet-gc-prod routes, the -bgsp
# form does not. Proof that EGT flip brands individually.
# Listed as DN_ILKBAHIS but routes under its casinokey name. Presumably a rebrand
# where EGT kept the original routing name.
# No -gc-prod or -gs-prod route on p3 or p4, in either naming form. Their
# -api-prod / -lobby-prod answer 502, which is not evidence the brand exists:
# a working brand returns the same 502 on its wrong cluster.
# Awaiting EGT confirmation; flip to yes and re-probe once they respond.
